scenes.animation: A post office counter. A cartoon postman holds up an envelope addressed in big shaky letters 'To God'. Zippy's eyes pop; the counter staff freeze mid-stamp.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Someone posted a letter to God? Which pin code is that?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: That is Lencho's letter. And the reply he gets is one of the finest ironies in your book.

scenes.animation: A lone house on the crest of a low hill above a valley; a ripe corn field dotted with flowers. Lencho stares at the sky; fat raindrops fall and turn into shiny coins labelled '10 cents' and '5 cents'. Then the drops harden into white hailstones and flatten the field.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Lencho is a farmer whose corn field only needs a downpour. The rain comes, and he calls the big drops ten-cent pieces and the little ones fives.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Then comes a hailstorm for an hour. The whole field is covered white and the crop is destroyed.

lines.speaker: LENCHO
lines.text: A plague of locusts would have left more than this.

scenes.animation: Night; Lencho's family sits sadly in the dim hut. Lencho writes by lamplight; the letter floats up: 'God, ... I need a hundred pesos.' It drops into a mailbox.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Lencho has one hope left: the help of God, whose eyes, he believes, see everything.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: So he writes to God, asking for a hundred pesos to sow his field again and to live until the new crop comes.

scenes.animation: The fat, amiable postmaster laughs, then turns serious. He passes a tin box around the office; coins drop in; he adds part of his own salary. A counter shows '70+ pesos'. He signs the reply 'God'.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: So the postmaster had a good laugh and binned it?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: He laughed first, but then he admired that faith and decided to reply. He collected money from his employees and friends and gave part of his own salary.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Even so, he could send only a little more than seventy pesos, signed with one word: God.

scenes.animation: Lencho counts the notes, frowns, and scribbles a second letter. Its words appear: 'Send me the rest... the post office employees are a bunch of crooks.' The postmaster's jaw drops; a big 'IRONY' stamp thumps onto the screen.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Lencho is not surprised to get money, but he is angry that it is short. God cannot make a mistake, he thinks, so someone stole it.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: His second letter asks God to send the rest, but not by mail, because the post office employees are a bunch of crooks.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: That is the irony: the kind people who helped him are the ones he blames.

scenes.animation: An exam paper slides in: 'Q. Who does Lencho think took the money? What is ironic about this?' Neo ticks three answer points: faith in God, blames postal staff, they were his real helpers. A 'Board Tip' sticker glows.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: A common board question: who does Lencho suspect, and what is ironic?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Answer approach: say he blames the post office employees, then explain that they were the very people who helped him.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Board tip: in a value question, mention both his unshakable faith and the postmaster's goodwill and charity.

scenes.animation: Recap board with a corn cob icon: '1. Hail destroys Lencho's crop', '2. Letter to God; postmaster sends 70+ pesos', '3. Irony: Lencho calls the helpers crooks'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap. One: a hailstorm destroys Lencho's corn crop.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: he writes to God for a hundred pesos, and the postmaster collects a little over seventy.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: in a twist of irony, Lencho calls his helpers a bunch of crooks.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Note to self: never post a thank-you letter to the wrong address.

name: Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom

scenes.animation: A packed amphitheatre at the Union Buildings in Pretoria, 10 May 1994. Jets roar overhead in formation; Zippy clutches a tiny South African flag and a paper cup of chai.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Air show, world leaders, two anthems. Is this a cricket final?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Bigger. It is the day Nelson Mandela takes oath as South Africa's first Black President.

scenes.animation: Mandela at the podium; beside him two figures labelled 'de Klerk: first Deputy President' and 'Thabo Mbeki: second Deputy President'. His words appear in gold: 'Never, never and never again...'. Two music notes float up labelled 'Nkosi Sikelel' iAfrika' and 'Die Stem'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: This excerpt is from his autobiography, Long Walk to Freedom. On the tenth of May, 1994, the first democratic, non-racial government is born.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Mandela promises that this beautiful land will never again experience the oppression of one by another.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The military jets that once stood for oppression now salute democracy, and two national anthems are sung, one by whites and one by blacks.

scenes.animation: A sepia timeline slides back through decades labelled 'Apartheid'. Then a weighing scale appears with 'Family' on one pan and 'People, community, country' on the other; the scale tips and a younger Mandela walks toward the second pan.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: He calls apartheid an extraordinary human disaster. It also produced heroes like Oliver Tambo and Walter Sisulu.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Every man has twin obligations: to his family, and to his people and country. Under apartheid, a Black man who tried to fulfil his duty to his people was punished and isolated.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: So he had to choose his country over his own family?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Exactly. That is the price he paid.

scenes.animation: Two chains shatter: one on a figure labelled 'Oppressed', one on a figure labelled 'Oppressor'. The line 'Courage is not the absence of fear, but the triumph over it' types out beside a glowing heart.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Mandela says the oppressor must be liberated just as surely as the oppressed. A man who takes away another's freedom is a prisoner of hatred.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: He learnt that courage was not the absence of fear, but the triumph over it.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: And no one is born hating another because of colour. People learn to hate, so they can be taught to love.

scenes.animation: An exam card: 'Q. What are the twin obligations Mandela mentions?' A two-column answer builds itself. A 'Board Tip' sticker flashes over the word 'apartheid'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Likely question: what twin obligations does Mandela mention, and why could he not fulfil both?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Answer approach: name both duties, then explain that apartheid punished anyone who served his people.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Board tip: define apartheid as a policy of racial discrimination in one line. Examiners love that clarity.

scenes.animation: Recap board with a rising sun over Pretoria: '1. 10 May 1994: first democratic, non-racial government', '2. Twin obligations: family and country', '3. Courage = triumph over fear; love can be taught'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap. One: on the tenth of May, 1994, Mandela became President of a democratic, non-racial South Africa.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: every man has twin obligations, to family and to country.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: courage is triumph over fear, and love comes more naturally to the human heart than hate.

scenes.animation: Split screen titled 'Two Stories about Flying'. Left: a scared young seagull on a cliff ledge. Right: an old Dakota plane in a storm cloud at night. Zippy bounces between them.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: One bird that won't fly and one pilot who can't see. Great combo.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two stories, one idea: facing fear. First, His First Flight by Liam O'Flaherty.

scenes.animation: The young seagull alone on the ledge; his brothers and sister soar over the sea. His parents circle, calling and scolding. His belly rumbles with a cartoon growl.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The young seagull's brothers and sister flew the day before, but he was afraid. The great sea seemed too wide for his little wings.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: His family taunted him and left him alone, and he had eaten nothing since the previous nightfall.

scenes.animation: The mother flies toward him with a piece of fish, then stops just out of reach. He dives for it with a scream, falls, then his wings spread and he soars; he lands on the green sea, feet sinking, as the family cheers and offers him scraps of dog-fish.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Then his mother flew toward him with a piece of fish and stopped just short of the ledge.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Maddened by hunger, he dived at the fish, fell outwards, and suddenly his wings spread. He was flying.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Hunger pushed him past fear. His family praised him and offered him scraps of dog-fish.

scenes.animation: Night sky. The narrator's old Dakota flies from Paris toward England; black storm clouds loom. Instruments spin, the radio crackles and dies, the fuel gauge drops. A black aeroplane with no lights appears alongside; its pilot waves.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Second story: The Black Aeroplane by Frederick Forsyth. A pilot flies his old Dakota to England, dreaming of a big English breakfast.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: He takes the risk of flying into a storm. His compass and other instruments stop working, the radio goes dead, and fuel runs low.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: A strange black aeroplane with no lights appears. Its pilot waves, and the narrator follows him to a runway.

scenes.animation: In a control room, a woman looks at the narrator with a puzzled face. A radar screen shows only one blip. A big question mark hangs over the empty sky.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: So he thanked the other pilot, right?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: He tried. But the woman in the control centre said there was no other aeroplane in the sky. His was the only one on the radar.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Board tip: for 'Who helped the narrator?' say it remains a mystery. Do not invent an answer.

scenes.animation: Recap board with a feather and a propeller: '1. Seagull: hunger overcomes fear of flying', '2. Pilot: storm, dead instruments, helped by a mystery plane', '3. Both: courage, risk, first steps'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap. One: the young seagull's hunger pushed him to make his first flight.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: the pilot was guided through a storm by a black aeroplane no one else saw.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: both stories show that facing fear and taking risks lead you home.

name: From the Diary of Anne Frank

scenes.animation: A cosy desk; a red-checked diary opens by itself and a name glows on the cover: 'Kitty'. Zippy tries to read it and Neo gently closes it.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Who names a diary Kitty?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Anne Frank did. She wanted the diary to be the true friend she never had.

scenes.animation: Anne at thirteen, surrounded by laughing classmates and a crowd labelled 'about 30 friends', yet a thought bubble shows her alone. A line appears: 'Paper has more patience than people.'

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Anne got the diary on her thirteenth birthday. She had loving parents, a sister and about thirty people she could call friends.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: But she could not confide in anyone deeply. So she wrote, because paper has more patience than people.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Thirty friends and still lonely? That makes no sense.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: It does. She says she could only talk about ordinary things with them, never share what was really in her heart.

scenes.animation: A quick family-history strip: Frankfurt to Holland in 1933 when Anne was four, a Montessori school, then the Jewish Lyceum. A small candle marks her grandmother's death, which Anne still feels deeply.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: She gives a short sketch of her life. Her family was Jewish and moved from Germany to Holland in 1933.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: She loved her grandmother deeply, and no one knew how often she still thought of her.

scenes.animation: A classroom. Mr Keesing, an old maths teacher, wags a finger: 'Essay: A Chatterbox'. Anne writes; then 'An Incorrigible Chatterbox'; then 'Quack, Quack, Quack, said Mistress Chatterback' appears as a poem with ducklings. Mr Keesing laughs.

lines.speaker: MR KEESING
lines.text: Miss Frank, you talk too much. Write an essay: A Chatterbox.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Anne argued that talking is a student's trait, and she had inherited it from her mother, who talked as much.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Then came An Incorrigible Chatterbox, and finally a poem about a mother duck and ducklings. Mr Keesing enjoyed the joke, and Anne was allowed to talk after that.

scenes.animation: An exam card: 'Q. How did Anne change Mr Keesing's attitude?' Three bullet points slide in: wit, logic, humour. A 'Board Tip' sticker appears.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Likely question: how did Anne win over Mr Keesing?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Answer approach: explain her logical first essay, the second one, and the funny poem that made him laugh.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Board tip: also be ready for why she called her diary Kitty and why she felt lonely despite many friends.

scenes.animation: Recap board with a diary icon: '1. Diary = Kitty, her true friend', '2. Lonely despite many friends', '3. Chatterbox essays and a poem win over Mr Keesing'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap. One: Anne named her diary Kitty and treated it as a true friend.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: she had many friends but no one to confide in.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: her wit turned a punishment into a win with Mr Keesing.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Great, now I have a reason to talk in class.

scenes.animation: A cartoon map of India lights up three spots: Goa, Coorg in Karnataka, and Assam. A bread loaf, a coffee cup and a tea leaf pop out of each.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Bread, coffee, tea. Is this a chapter or a breakfast menu?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Both! Glimpses of India has three parts: a baker from Goa, Coorg, and tea from Assam.

scenes.animation: A Goan village morning. A plump baker in a knee-length frock (label 'kabai') walks with a jingling bamboo staff; children run to him. A wall shows pencil tally marks for monthly bills. Labels pop up: 'bol - marriages', 'bolinhas - Christmas'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: In A Baker from Goa, Lucio Rodrigues remembers the pader, the baker from Portuguese times. The jingling thud of his bamboo staff woke everyone.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Marriage gifts were meaningless without the sweet bread called bol, and bolinhas were a must at Christmas.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The baker wore a kabai, and bills were recorded on a wall in pencil. Bakers were prosperous, and their plump physique showed it.

scenes.animation: Misty hills, coffee estates and a river. A proud Kodava in a long black coat with an embroidered waist-belt labelled 'kuppia'. Icons pop: river rafting, Brahmagiri hills, Buddhist monks at Bylakuppe.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Coorg, by Lokesh Abrol, is a district of Karnataka, a land of rolling hills, coffee estates and the Kaveri river.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Its people, the Kodavus, are known for martial traditions and hospitality. One story says they may be of Greek or Arabic descent.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: They are the only people in India permitted to carry firearms without a licence.

scenes.animation: A train rattles through green tea gardens. Rajvir and Pranjol look out; workers pluck leaves into bamboo baskets. A legend panel shows leaves falling into an emperor's boiling pot, and another shows a monk with ten tea plants.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: In Tea from Assam, Rajvir travels with his friend Pranjol, whose father manages a tea garden in Assam.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Rajvir shares two legends: a Chinese emperor whose boiling water got a few leaves, and Bodhidharma, from whose eyelids ten tea plants grew.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Assam has the largest concentration of tea plantations in the world.

scenes.animation: An exam card: 'Q. What do we learn about the Kodavus?' or 'Q. Why were bakers important in Goa?' A 'Board Tip' sticker points at the word 'descent'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Likely questions: how were Goan bakers linked to festivals, or what makes the Kodavus special?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Board tip: write two or three exact details from the text, such as the bol, the kabai, or the kuppia.

scenes.animation: Recap board: '1. Goa: the pader, bol and bolinhas', '2. Coorg: coffee, Kaveri, the brave Kodavus', '3. Assam: tea legends and the largest tea plantations'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap. One: the Goan baker is part of every festival and celebration.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: Coorg is a land of coffee, hills and the brave Kodavus.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: Assam grows tea on a huge scale, and tea comes with fascinating legends.

scenes.animation: An aircraft cabin in chaos: a sleek otter darts between seats, a passenger stands on her seat shrieking, and an air hostess stays calm. Zippy hides in a cup holder.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Why is there a furry torpedo on this plane?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: That is Mijbil, Gavin Maxwell's pet otter. Let's see how he got there.

scenes.animation: Southern Iraq, 1956. Maxwell unpacks at the Consulate-General in Basra; a sack wriggles, and out comes a small otter. The name 'Mijbil' writes itself in the air.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: In 1956, Maxwell went to Southern Iraq and decided he wanted an otter as a pet. Soon one was delivered to him in a sack at Basra.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: He named it Mijbil. It turned out to be a race of otter unknown to science, later called Maxwell's otter.

scenes.animation: Mij splashes wildly in a bathtub, then plays with a rubber ball, juggling marbles on his belly. Water sprays all over the bathroom floor.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Mij was aloof at first, but soon he followed Maxwell everywhere. He loved water, rolling and splashing in the bathtub.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: He even invented games with a rubber ball and marbles, playing for hours.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: So he was basically a furry toddler with a swimming pool obsession.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Pretty much. He would even shuffle a rubber ball round the room like a four-footed footballer.

scenes.animation: An airline rule card: 'Animals must travel in a box'. Mij tears the box lining in a panic, bloodied; Maxwell opens it on the plane and Mij escapes, causing chaos. A kind air hostess helps Maxwell.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Flying to London, the airline required Mij to travel in a box. Mij fought the box, tearing its lining, and hurt himself.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: When Maxwell opened it, Mij escaped and ran about the cabin until he was caught. A kind air hostess helped them through.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The story shows how an animal, treated with love and patience, becomes a true companion.

scenes.animation: A London street. People stare at Mij on a leash and guess: 'baby seal?', 'squirrel?', 'beaver?', 'bear cub?', 'hippo?'. Zippy laughs at each speech bubble.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Did Londoners at least know what he was?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Not at all. People guessed a baby seal, a squirrel, a beaver, a bear cub, even a hippo.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Board tip: questions often ask about Mij's water games and the guesses of Londoners. Use these specific details.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: A second question may ask how Maxwell handled the crisis on the plane. Mention his calm and the air hostess's kindness.

scenes.animation: Recap board with an otter icon: '1. Mijbil: a rare otter from Iraq', '2. Loved water and play', '3. Chaotic flight; Londoners puzzled'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap. One: Mijbil was a rare otter Maxwell brought from Iraq.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: he loved water and invented his own games.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: the journey to London was chaotic, and nobody there knew what he was.

scenes.animation: A village doorway. Eight-year-old Valli watches a bus roar past, her eyes sparkling. A piggy bank labelled '60 paise' fills coin by coin as she refuses peppermints and a merry-go-round.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Why is she saving every coin like she's buying a car?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Because Valli wants to ride the bus to town, all by herself. The story is by Vallikkannan.

scenes.animation: Valli boards the bus when her mother naps in the afternoon. The conductor bows playfully: 'Madam'. She pays thirty paise and presses her face to the window.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: She collects facts about the bus, then saves sixty paise, enough for the return fare.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: One afternoon she boards alone. The conductor, amused by her confidence, calls her Madam.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Thirty paise each way. That is two peppermints she gave up, at least.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: She gave up much more. She resisted sweets, toys and even a merry-go-round ride to save that money.

scenes.animation: Through the window: canals, palm trees, a green countryside. A young cow runs ahead of the bus with its tail up; Valli laughs out loud. An elderly woman tries to talk; Valli turns away.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: She enjoys everything outside. A young cow running in front of the bus makes her laugh.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: She refuses to be treated as a child and even snubs an elderly woman who calls her too young to travel alone.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: When the conductor teases her, she replies smartly. She wants to be treated as a grown-up passenger.

scenes.animation: In town she stays on the bus and refuses a free drink from the conductor. On the way back, the same young cow lies dead on the roadside; colours drain from the scene.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: In town, she doesn't get off and even refuses a free drink, because she has no money to spare.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: On the return trip, she sees the same young cow lying dead by the road. Her joy vanishes, and she no longer wants to look out.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Back home, she does not tell her mother. Her secret adventure has ended with a quiet lesson.

scenes.animation: An exam card: 'Q. How did the dead cow change Valli's mood?' Answer points: first encounter with death, growing up, sadness. A 'Board Tip' sticker appears.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Likely question: what effect did the dead cow have on Valli?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Answer approach: link the happy sight of the cow on the way to her first sad brush with death on the way back.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Board tip: also mention her independence and self-respect, like paying her own fare and refusing favours.

scenes.animation: Recap board with a bus icon: '1. Valli saves 60 paise to ride alone', '2. Independent and curious', '3. The dead cow = first experience of death'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap. One: Valli plans and saves for her first bus journey.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: she is curious, independent and proud.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: the dead cow gives her a first, painful lesson about death.

scenes.animation: A grieving young mother carries her lifeless child door to door, asking for medicine. Neighbours shake their heads. Zippy's spark dims in sympathy.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Can nobody help her?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Someone will, but not in the way she expects. This is Kisa Gotami, and the teacher is the Buddha.

scenes.animation: A quick timeline of Prince Siddhartha Gautama: palace life, then four sights appear one by one: a sick man, an aged man, a funeral procession, a monk begging. He leaves the palace and meditates under a large tree labelled 'Bodhi Tree'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Prince Siddhartha Gautama was shielded from suffering. Then he saw a sick man, an aged man, a funeral and a monk begging for alms.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: He left his palace to seek enlightenment. After meditating under a tree, he became the Buddha, the Awakened or Enlightened One.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: He preached his first sermon at Benares.

scenes.animation: The Buddha speaks kindly to Kisa Gotami: 'Bring a handful of mustard seed.' A label appears: 'from a house where no one has lost a child, husband, parent or friend'. She walks through lamp-lit lanes, each door answering 'We have lost someone'.

lines.speaker: KISA GOTAMI
lines.text: Please, give me medicine for my son.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The Buddha asked Kisa Gotami for a handful of mustard seed, but from a house where no one had lost a child, husband, parent or friend.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Every house had mustard seed, but every house had also lost someone.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: So the Buddha gave her a task that could never be finished?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Yes, on purpose. He wanted her to discover the truth herself, not just hear it.

scenes.animation: Evening; lights in houses flicker and go out one by one. Kisa Gotami sits by the roadside, understanding dawns on her face. A glowing line: 'The living are few, but the dead are many.'

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Sitting by the roadside, she saw lights flicker and go out. She realised death is common to all, and her grief had been selfish.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The Buddha taught that the wise do not grieve, knowing the terms of the world. Grief only brings more pain.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The message: accept that all living beings must die, and find peace instead of endless sorrow.

scenes.animation: An exam card: 'Q. Why did the Buddha send Kisa Gotami for mustard seed?' Answer points build: impossible condition, discovers universality of death, peace. A 'Board Tip' sticker appears.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Likely question: why did the Buddha send her from house to house?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Answer approach: he wanted her to discover for herself that death is universal, so she could let go of selfish grief.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Board tip: do not write that the mustard seed was a medicine. It was a lesson.

scenes.animation: Recap board with a lamp icon: '1. Siddhartha's four sights lead to enlightenment', '2. Mustard seed task for Kisa Gotami', '3. Death is universal; do not grieve selfishly'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap. One: seeing suffering led Siddhartha to become the Buddha.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: he gave Kisa Gotami an impossible task with mustard seed.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: she learnt that death is universal, and wise people accept it.

scenes.animation: A Russian country drawing room. Lomov, in evening dress and white gloves, clutches his chest nervously. Chubukov greets him suspiciously. A curtain labels 'A one-act play by Anton Chekhov'.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Why is he dressed like a wedding cake?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Because Lomov has come to propose to Natalya, the daughter of his neighbour Chubukov.

scenes.animation: Lomov fidgets, clutches his heart and taps a sleepy foot. Chubukov happily hugs him and runs off to call Natalya. Three name tags: 'Chubukov - landowner', 'Natalya - his daughter, 25', 'Lomov - neighbour, 35, hypochondriac'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Lomov is thirty-five, a critical age, he says. He is nervous, and always complains of palpitations.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Chubukov is delighted by the proposal and sends Natalya in, but he doesn't tell her why Lomov has come.

lines.speaker: LOMOV
lines.text: I must make up my mind. If I wait for my ideal or for real love, I will never get married.

scenes.animation: A map of land labelled 'Oxen Meadows' between two estates. Lomov and Natalya pull the map like a tug-of-war; Chubukov jumps in, threatening lawsuits.

lines.speaker: LOMOV
lines.text: The Oxen Meadows are mine!

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Before Lomov can propose, he mentions the Oxen Meadows, and both claim them. The quarrel turns into insults.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: When Natalya learns he came to propose, she wails for him to be brought back.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Wait, she wanted him back after calling him names?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Instantly. That sudden change shows how practical, and how comic, the whole match really is.

scenes.animation: Round two: two cartoon dogs labelled 'Guess' and 'Squeezer' appear with price tags. Lomov faints dramatically; Chubukov pushes them together: 'Here's your bride!' Champagne pops as they argue again.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: He returns, but now they fight over whose dog is better, Lomov's Guess or Natalya's Squeezer.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Lomov collapses. Chubukov hurries them into agreeing to marry, and they immediately start quarrelling again.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Chekhov is satirising marriages made for property and convenience, not love.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Every character is quick to take offence, and Chekhov uses that to make us laugh at them.

scenes.animation: An exam card: 'Q. What were the two quarrels about?' and 'Q. How is the play a satire?' A 'Board Tip' sticker points at the word 'satire'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Likely questions: what did Lomov and Natalya quarrel about, and what does the play mock?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Answer approach: name the Oxen Meadows and the dogs, then explain the satire on greed and quarrelsome landowners.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Board tip: use character sketches with evidence, like Lomov's palpitations and Natalya's instant change when she hears 'proposal'.

scenes.animation: Recap board with a wedding ring and two dog bones: '1. Lomov comes to propose to Natalya', '2. Quarrels: Oxen Meadows, then Guess vs Squeezer', '3. Satire on marriage for property'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap. One: nervous Lomov comes to propose to Natalya.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: they quarrel over the Oxen Meadows and then over their dogs.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: the comedy mocks marriage for property and constant bickering.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Lesson learnt: propose first, discuss dogs later.
